message.abstract: <jats:sec><jats:title>Objective</jats:title><jats:p>To assess whether physicians' reported electronic health record (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content>) use provides clinical benefits and whether benefits depend on using an <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> meeting Meaningful Use criteria or length of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> experience.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Data Source</jats:title><jats:p>The 2011 Physician Workflow study, representative of U.S. office‐based physicians.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Study Design</jats:title><jats:p>Cross‐sectional data were used to examine the association of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> use with enhanced patient care overall and nine specific clinical benefits.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Principal Findings</jats:title><jats:p>Most physicians with <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content>s reported <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> use enhanced patient care overall (78 percent), helped them access a patient's chart remotely (81 percent), and alerted them to a potential medication error (65 percent) and critical lab values (62 percent). Between 30 and 50 percent of physicians reported that <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> use was associated with clinical benefits related to providing recommended care, ordering appropriate tests, and facilitating patient communication. Using <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content>s that met Meaningful Use criteria and having 2 or more years of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> experience were independently associated with reported benefits. Physicians with <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content>s meeting Meaningful Use criteria and longer <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> experience were most likely to report benefits across all 10 measures.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title><jats:p>Physicians reported <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> use enhanced patient care overall. Clinical benefits were most likely to be reported by physicians using <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content>s meeting Meaningful Use criteria and longer <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">EHR</jats:styled-content> experience.</jats:p></jats:sec>
title: Clinical Benefits of Electronic Health Record Use: National Findings
